situated_beneficiary.person_or_government: MK Haim Ramon (Kadima), a sitting member of the 17th Knesset on the day of passage
situated_beneficiary.matter: The pending criminal proceeding against Ramon: convicted on 31.1.2007 of an indecent act, with the court's determination on moral turpitude and the sentence still pending on 20–21.3.2007, so the judgment was not final. The replaced s. 42B(a) makes suspension from the Knesset automatic from the day a court finds turpitude until the judgment becomes final, in place of the Knesset Committee's discretion, and would operate directly on that pending matter.
situated_beneficiary.admissible_fact: Item 1: a proceeding pending before a court concerning that person. Knesset Constitution, Law and Justice Committee protocol no. 170 of 20.3.2007, the session preparing this bill (כ/125, P/17/413) for second and third reading: the chair stated that MK Ramon had been convicted, that whether the court would find turpitude was still open, and that if it did the law would apply to him if passed the next day.
situated_beneficiary.source: Protocol no. 170, Constitution, Law and Justice Committee, 17th Knesset, 20.3.2007 (Knesset record; mirror production.oknesset.org/.../135054.DOC); conviction date from the dateline of an nrg/Maariv report (makorrishon.co.il/nrg/online/1/ART1/537/704.html, last updated 31/1/2007) as shown in a search summary; enactment text ס"ח 2090, 28.3.2007 (archived Knesset PDF 17_lsr_300071); pre-amendment s. 42B from the sheet's archived Nevo page
situated_beneficiary.support: חבר הכנסת רמון הורשע, והשאלה במתח באוויר אם הוא יורשע עם עבירה שיש עמה קלון
situated_beneficiary.list_version: (ae), adopted 2026-10-22, as clarified by (af) the same day
situated_beneficiary.note: Operative provisions: s. 42B(a) replaced (automatic suspension on a court's turpitude finding until finality), s. 42B(b) made automatic for an MK sentenced to imprisonment, s. 42B(c) repealed. Pre-amendment text (Nevo history): the Knesset Committee 'may', on any MK's proposal, suspend a convicted MK while the judgment is not final. The alteration in the live matter: for the one sitting MK with a non-final conviction, suspension pending finality ceased to depend on the Knesset Committee and became automatic upon a turpitude finding; the protocol identifies no other 17th-Knesset MK with a non-final conviction. The sponsor's stated motive in the protocol (a Likud candidate convicted during the 2006 campaign) is excluded as motive. I did not use, and did not open any page describing, the court's eventual turpitude determination (see deviations). The gazette footnote prints the bill's publication date as 8.1.2008, a misprint for 2007.

situated_beneficiary.person_or_government: The 33rd government (Netanyahu), sworn in on 18.3.2013, the day before passage
situated_beneficiary.matter: The 2013 state budget, not yet tabled: the deadline for the government to table the 2013 budget bill and the 'determining day' (s. 36A, Basic Law: The Knesset) on which the Knesset would be deemed dissolved if the budget had not passed.
situated_beneficiary.admissible_fact: Item 3: a fixed deadline that the enactment moves, binding the sitting government. Under s. 36A(b) of Basic Law: The Knesset as then in force, after elections the determining day was three months from the start of the fiscal year (1.4.2013) or 45 days from the government's formation (18.3.2013, i.e. 2.5.2013), whichever is later; new s. 4(b) of the temporary Basic Law fixes the determining day for the 2013 budget at 31.7.2013, and new s. 4(a) requires the government to table the 2013 budget bill by 11.6.2013 (existing s. 3(b)(1) of Basic Law: The State Economy then contained no special rule for a post-election year). Item 4 also: the new Chapter B is headed 'special provisions for the budget for 2013', a single-instance clause applying to the sitting government's own budget bill.
situated_beneficiary.source: Enactment text, ס"ח 2391, 20.3.2013 (archived Knesset PDF 19_lsr_301538); Basic Law: The Knesset s. 36A(b) pre-2014 text from the sheet's archived Nevo page (amendment history with strike/underline markup); Basic Law: The State Economy s. 3(b)(1) history, Nevo; INN (Arutz 7) report 'הושבעה הממשלה ה-33 של מדינת ישראל', 18.3.2013

situated_beneficiary.matter: The ability of serving ministers and deputy ministers to resign their Knesset seats and be replaced from their lists with return rights during the 20th Knesset (the 'Norwegian law'), and the exemption of deputy ministers already in office from the new oath.
situated_beneficiary.admissible_fact: Item 4: a sunset clause in the enactment itself. Section 6 (הוראת שעה): ss. 23, 42C and 43 of Basic Law: The Knesset and ss. 26(5), 30A and 30B of Basic Law: The Government, as enacted here, and s. 5(b), apply during the term of the 20th Knesset only. Section 5 (הוראת מעבר) applies only to deputy ministers appointed before commencement. The sunset covers the term during which the sitting government holds office; ministers of governments formed after later Knesset elections do not share it.
situated_beneficiary.source: Enactment text, ס"ח 2500, 6.8.2015, pp. 248–250 (archived Knesset PDF 20_lsr_313649); Kipa report 'לאחר סערות ועיכובים: הממשלה ה-34 יוצאת לדרך', 14.5.2015 (government approved 61–59, Netanyahu PM); Walla report 7.5.2015 on the coalition's formation

(a2) binds the Finance Minister to submit a detailed plan by 1.5.2020 and the government to table it. The measure is the sitting government's own 2020 expenditure; existing s. 3B gave only one-twelfth of the previous budget.

situated_beneficiary.person_or_government: The 37th government (Netanyahu; Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, named in the Knesset Legal Adviser's letter of 18.1.2024), in office throughout October–December 2023
situated_beneficiary.matter: The government's failure to submit the 'differences report' for the 2024 budget year by 1.11.2023 under s. 3A1(a)(2) and the consequential balancing-plan deadlines (1.12.2023 onward), and its pending request to defer them (government bill tabled 23.10.2023, 'חוק-יסוד: משק המדינה (הוראת שעה לעניין חוק התקציב לשנת 2024 – חרבות ברזל)', proposing the report by 15.12.2023 and the balancing-plan notice by 26.12.2023).
situated_beneficiary.admissible_fact: Item 2: a formal step already taken against the government's measure. The Knesset Legal Adviser's letter of 26.11.2023 to the Finance Ministry's legal adviser, headed 'non-compliance with the convergence mechanism in s. 3A1', records that the report had not been submitted, that the Finance Committee on 30.10.2023 declined to advance the government's deferral bill, and states that as long as the report is not submitted the government is not complying with the Basic Law and that reports must be submitted to avoid continued breach. The operative provision passed on 14.12.2023, new s. 3A1(a1), empowers the government, with Knesset approval on the Finance Committee's recommendation, to defer the report deadline and the other s. 3A1 dates by up to 50 days after an exceptional and unforeseen event with significant fiscal impact, counting the automatic-cut date from the date fixed in s. 7 of the Fiscal Adjustments Law, 2023; on the day of passage it operated directly on the sitting government's already-missed 2024-cycle deadlines.
situated_beneficiary.source: Knesset Legal Adviser (Sagit Afik), letter ref. 2023-091777 of 26.11.2023 (Knesset record; mirror next.obudget.org/datapackages/knesset/knesset_legal_advisor_letters/9763047053c4b860.pdf); operative text of s. 3A1(a1) from Nevo consolidated Basic Law: The State Economy, marked 'תיקון מס' 14, ס"ח תשפ"ד 3127, 17.12.2023, עמ' 278 (ה"ח 1661)'; passage date 14.12.2023 and the permanent form of the enactment from the Knesset Legal Adviser's letters of 11.1.2024 and 18.1.2024 (same mirror), read only for those facts

situated_beneficiary.note: Items 3 and 4 are not met on the text as passed: the enactment does not itself move a date (it confers a power, which the Knesset exercised on 20.12.2023, after passage) and, per the Knesset Legal Adviser's letter of 18.1.2024, the government's temporary-provision bill was converted in committee into a permanent provision, so the enactment contains no single-instance or sunset clause. Yes rests on item 2 (a formal step against the government's measure, analogous to an attorney general's opinion) and on the sheet's rule that a provision general in form is Yes where it has direct legal effect on a pending matter to which only the sitting government is party; an adjudicator who confines item 2 to the three listed examples would code No. The published gazette text (ס"ח 3127) and the bill (ה"ח 1661) could not be obtained (Knesset site geo-blocked; no Wayback capture); the text is taken from Nevo, whose header lists no commencement or temporary clause for this amendment. The sheet's date for this row is the publication date; passage was 14.12.2023.
